ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In order to explore the action of auxin, corn coleoptile segments with the tips removed were randomly divided into two groups. In the experimental group, an agar block containing an appropriate concentration of IAA was placed on one side of the upper end of the coleoptile; in the control group, an agar block without IAA was placed on the same side of the upper end of the coleoptile. The coleoptiles of the two groups were kept under the same conditions in the dark for a period of time. Afterward, the coleoptiles in the control group showed no curved growth, while the coleoptiles in the experimental group underwent curved growth, as shown in the figure. Judge according to the experimental results. Is the amount of IAA obtained by agar block d′ from a′ less than or greater than the output amount of a′?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure, the coleoptile on the left is in a vertical state, with agar block a placed on one side of the upper end, and the lower end contacting agar block d; after being placed for a period of time, the coleoptile on the right has bent, the agar block on one side of the upper end is labeled a′, and the agar block collected at the lower end is labeled d′. Then reason: in the experimental group, a′ contains an appropriate concentration of IAA, while the control group does not contain IAA and does not bend, indicating that the bending of the experimental group is caused by IAA in a′ entering the coleoptile and promoting elongation on one side. After the IAA output by a′ enters the coleoptile, part of it will diffuse in the coleoptile tissue, be retained, or be absorbed by cells and exert the effect of promoting growth, and only the remaining part continues to be transported downward and enters d′. Therefore, the amount of IAA obtained by agar block d′ from a′ is less than the output amount of a′.
